title: Qualitative research methods: how to choose the right one for your market research
summary: Learn which qualitative research methods fit which questions, with a simple framework for choosing the right one.
body_markdown:
What is a qualitative research method? +


A qualitative research method is a way of collecting and analyzing non-numerical data to understand how people experience and make sense of something. It gives researchers a more detailed view than numerical data alone can provide.


How do you choose the right qualitative research method? +


Start with what you need to learn and choose the method that can answer that question most directly. The "How to choose a qualitative research method" section in this article compares methods based on the type of insight they can provide and how the research is carried out.


What is the difference between qualitative and quantitative research methods? +


Qualitative research uses non-numerical data to explore a research question in depth. Quantitative methods use numerical data to measure something and identify patterns. Mixed methods research combines both approaches when a study needs both qualitative and quantitative data.


Can AI-moderated interviews replace traditional qualitative research methods? +


AI-moderated interviews can help researchers conduct interviews at greater scale while keeping the research focused on real participants. They extend the researcher's reach, and the study design, judgment and interpretation stay with the researcher.


Can you combine qualitative research methods in one study? +


Yes. A study that combines qualitative methods can look at different aspects of the same question, like following interviews with a diary study to see whether what people describe holds up over several weeks. Drawing on more than one data source gives deeper insights and makes it easier to draw conclusions stakeholders will trust.


What are grounded theory and narrative research in qualitative research? +


Grounded theory and narrative research are two other qualitative methods, more common in academic and social sciences research than in commercial studies. Grounded theory researchers collect and analyze data at the same time to generate hypotheses from the data itself, and keep going until new data stops adding anything, known as theoretical saturation. Narrative research focuses on the stories people tell about their lives to understand how they make sense of human experience.
